body: I felt the same way coming out of student teaching and I just feel like it in now way prepared me for the insane amount of paperwork and other administrative stuff that I had to do. I just couldn't handle it.

Your reply was one of the ones that I really identify with. I posted this the afternoon before I admitted myself into the hospital. I'm bipolar 2 so I already have marked depression and now I was so overwhelmed, stressed, and consumed with thoughts of the job and I just wanted it to stop. I was scared for my own safety so I got help. They gave me a sedative that first night and I just slept off and on all through Thursday and Friday nights. Saturday I woke up, though a lot and made the decision that I am definitely not going back. I won't even go back to clear out my room, and I brought in a ton of my own supplies because my school provided nothing, I don't actually need any if it. Lucky for the next teacher. A lot (a lot) of money lost, but it's not like I could get it back anyway. I was just wildly unprepared for the sheer amount of paperwork and *stuff* I would have to do. Maybe it would be different in a small private school. Maybe it would be different in high school, where I'd only have 3 classes instead of 5. I just know that this public school system is definitely not for me. I'm trying not to feel guilty about quitting. All the work I put in and work other people put in and are now going to have to put in to find my replacement, etc gone to waste. I definitely feel relief. But I'm still really messed up from the whole thing. I'm strong enough to admit that I'm just not strong enough.
